whatItIs.text: Immature soybeans boiled or steamed in the pod and salted — a snack and side across East and Southeast Asia.

historyNote.text: Soybeans were first cultivated in China some 7,000 years ago; the first written mention of 'edamame' is a note from 1275 in which the Japanese monk Nichiren thanks a parishioner for a gift of them.

howToChoose.text: Frozen pods are the standard buy — look for bright green, undamaged pods without freezer frost; shelled 'mukimame' saves a step in the kitchen.

storage.text: Keep frozen until cooking; leftover cooked beans keep covered in the fridge.

foodSafetyRef.note: Practice storage guidance only; no rulebook content is claimed. The app's food-safety rules live in data/food-safety/rules.json.

useItUp.text: Boil straight from frozen for 3-4 minutes, salt generously, and squeeze the beans out; shelled leftovers join fried rice, grain bowls, and salads.
